Eras Tour
EER-uz TOOR
proper noun (Gen Alpha slang)
Taylor Swift’s concert tour of March 2023 to December 2024: 149 shows on five continents, each about three and a half hours long and organized into "eras" — one for each of her albums. It became the highest-grossing concert tour in history, reported at over two billion dollars, and a cultural event: a ticket-site crash in November 2022 led to a U.S. Senate hearing, cities reported a "Swift lift" in local business, a Seattle crowd’s dancing registered on seismographs (July 2023), and a concert film followed in October 2023. It gave Gen Alpha the phrase "my ___ era" for any phase of life.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Eras Tour was Taylor Swift’s giant 2023–24 concert tour, and many Gen Alpha girls either went, watched the movie, or traded bracelets with someone who did. It also gave them a new phrase: "I’m in my ___ era" — my reading era, my soccer era, my villain era. The Christian observation: thinking of life in eras is close to how Scripture thinks, but with one great difference. Our lives do have seasons: "My times are in thy hand" (Psa 31:15), and God "changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings" (Dan 2:21). A child moving from one season to another is moving under God’s hand, not reinventing herself by choice. And the difference is this: God Himself has no eras. "Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever" (Heb 13:8). Pop stars change looks and sounds every album; the Lord never needs a new era, because He is perfect already. A father can tell a five-year-old: "People have eras — you’re in your kindergarten era! But Jesus is always the same. He loved you yesterday, He loves you today, and He’ll love you forever." The phrase "villain era" deserves a gentler correction: Christians do not have villain eras; we have repentance.

Webster 1828 Definition

Taylor Swift’s record-grossing 2023–24 tour of album "eras," source of "my ___ era" — lives in seasons under God’s hand, before the Christ who has no eras.

ERAS TOUR, proper n. (Taylor Swift concert tour, March 2023-December 2024; Gen Alpha usage) The tour, its film, and its culture. "My cousin went to the Eras Tour!"

Phrase spread: my ___ era — a phase of life ("my reading era," "my villain era").

Records and events: highest-grossing tour; 2022 ticketing crash and Senate hearing; "Swift Quake" (Seattle, 2023); concert film (2023).

Decode for parents: the event was mostly wholesome spectacle; the "era" talk is worth a conversation about identity.

Webster 1828, the root — ERA, n. In chronology, a fixed point of time, from which any number of years is begun to be counted; as the Christian era It differs from epoch in this; era is a point of time fixed by some nation or denomination of men; epoch is a point fixed by historians and chronologists.

Webster 1828, the root — TOUR, n. Literally, a going round; hence, a journey in a circuit; as the tour of Europe; the tour of France or England.

Key Scripture

Psa 31:15 — "My times are in thy hand: deliver me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me."

Dan 2:21 — "And he changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding:"

Heb 13:8 — "Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever."

Ecc 3:1 — "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:"

Modern Corruption

The Eras Tour taught a generation to narrate life as self-chosen reinventions; Scripture places our seasons in God’s hand and fixes our hope on the Christ who is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

expand to see more

The tour itself was mostly bright spectacle. The idea it popularized — life as a series of self-curated eras, each with its own aesthetic — is a quiet theology of the self: I reinvent myself, and each version is valid. The "villain era" variant even makes a season of sin into a style. Children absorb that framing early.

Give the better frame. Seasons are real, and God appoints them; growth is real, and God works it. The Christian story has a beginning, a turning point (repentance and faith), and a destination — not a set of costumes. And at its center is the One who never changes, so that His children can change toward Him.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin aera (counters, an epoch) → English era + French tour → the Eras Tour (2023–24) → "my ___ era."

expand to see more

Late Latin aera — a fixed date, an epoch → English era

French tour — a turn, a circuit

March 17, 2023: first show (Glendale, Arizona)

December 8, 2024: final show (Vancouver); 149 shows total

Phrase: "my ___ era"

Usage

""I’m in my baking era." "Your times are in His hand — bake on.""

"Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever — no eras (Heb 13:8)."

"To every thing there is a season — and God sets them (Ecc 3:1)."
